proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a same-class nuisance-sensitive interaction lower envelope, a strict non-oracle tuple, an oracle submodel reduction, a finite-grid KR projection result, and a comparator-separation witness; the mathematical reviewer reported no errors in those results. The attempted finite-order higher-order estimator did not obtain joint negative-Besov coefficient control once the covariate projection rank exceeds the sample size. Consequently the full matched rate, attaining estimator, critical logarithms, and necessary-and-sufficient oracle boundary remain open, so the sound partial paper cannot stand in for the fixed theorem kernel.
tldr: The known-uniform-design benchmark isolates a way marginal counterfactual generation can be harder than direct smooth-density estimation: the same rough propensity field is reused across all outcome locations even though the covariate distribution itself is known. The target is marginal-mixture \(W_1\), which is strictly weaker than GANICE's design-averaged statewise extended Wasserstein loss; an explicit smooth separation prevents importing that paper's lower bound or continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory, while convexity preserves a one-way, generally nonsharp upper-bound implication. The project asks for the complete minimax expected \(W_1\) frontier over this positive sectional-Hölder class, including critical logarithms and an if-and-only-if oracle boundary. Its proved negative side uses a shared-sign causal mixture whose marginal transport separation survives covariate averaging; its proposed positive side requires simultaneous finite-order correction of a growing outcome-wavelet dictionary followed by finite Kantorovich--Rubinstein projection. The representative legal tuple \(d=1,m=6,s=4,\alpha=\beta=27/200\) yields the proposed lower exponent \(243/697\), strictly slower than both scalar and oracle comparators. The full asymmetric known-design match, not that isolated bound or a claim about general factual generators, is the headline open content.
gap: Even with the covariate law fixed and known to be uniform, DoubleGen's oracle transfer and first-order nuisance bound do not determine whether rough propensity and treated conditional-density sections enlarge marginal \(W_1\) risk. GANICE develops continuous-conditioning minimax upper/lower theory for design-averaged statewise Wasserstein loss, matched only up to logarithmic and implementation-transfer factors, but a smooth positive pair can have positive statewise-average distance and identical marginal mixtures, so its lower bound and continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory do not settle this target. Direct \(W_1\) density theory removes confounding, fixed counterfactual-density projections do not reconstruct a refining law, and the public ACIC 2023 announcement does not expose a theorem that settles this exact known-design multivariate loss.
fill: A shared-propensity multiscale lower construction is matched by a high-rank higher-order coefficient estimator that exploits the known uniform basis geometry and by a finite probability projection. The resulting known-design marginal-mixture theorem provides every non-oracle rate, every critical logarithm, and the necessary-and-sufficient oracle boundary, without claiming a frontier for unknown-design factual generators or importing an extended-loss converse.
